item.title: Chick-fil-A is one of America's toughest franchises, and the startup cost may shock you
item.description: Julian Good reveals Chick-fil-A's $10,000 franchise fee and the staggering odds facing 100,000 yearly applicants vying for roughly 200 spots.
item.content:encoded:
Chick-fil-A is one of America's toughest franchises to get, attracting thousands of hopeful applicants each year for a limited number of owner-operator opportunities.

The fast-food chain's unique business model was recently highlighted by Julian Good, who owns a Chick-fil-A restaurant in St. Charles, Illinois, during an appearance on the "Founder Talk" podcast.

"It's a $10,000 franchise fee. It's been the same for the last 50 years," Good said.

CHICK-FIL-A COPYCAT RECIPE REVEALED AS CEO SHARES INGREDIENT THAT MAKES IT TASTE LIKE THE ORIGINAL

About 100,000 people apply each year to become a Chick-fil-A owner-operator, with roughly 200 ultimately selected, Good explained.

Applicants without Chick-fil-A experience often wait three to five years before receiving an opportunity, he added.

Chick-fil-A describes its selection process as "highly competitive," saying it looks for leaders willing to devote their full-time and best efforts to operating a restaurant, according to Chick-fil-A’s January 2024 post on its press room website.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

However, previous experience with the company isn't required.

More than 25% of newly selected owner-operators had never worked at one of its restaurants or for the company before applying, according to Chick-fil-A.

The company said operators also come from a wide range of professional backgrounds, including manufacturing, health care, education, law enforcement and retail.

Unlike many franchise systems, Chick-fil-A owner-operators do not own the restaurant they operate, according to Franchise Business Review. Chick-fil-A retains ownership of the restaurant, equipment, and, in most cases, the real estate, meaning operators do not build equity in the business or sell it when they retire.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Chick-fil-A said operators devote their time and energy to managing their restaurants, developing employees and serving their communities.

Good said that's one of the biggest differences between Chick-fil-A and many competing franchise models.

"When a Chick-fil-A operator retires, you can't pass it down to your kids. You don't sell the business or anything. It just goes back into the hands of Chick-fil-A," he said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Chick-fil-A's unique approach also extends to its operating schedule, with all of its restaurants closed on Sundays.

The weekly tradition remains an important part of the company's culture, Good noted.

"Just a way to glorify God and give back to the team and the community," he said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Chick-fil-A for comment.

item.title: Trump says Lindsay Clancy case is a ‘state situation' following attorney's pardon plea
item.description: President Donald Trump expressed sympathy for the family of Lindsay Clancy’s three children while signaling that he would not intervene in the former nurse’s state murder case.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump on Sunday signaled that he would not intervene in the case of Massachusetts mother Lindsay Clancy, who is charged with killing her three young children amid allegations that she suffered from postpartum psychosis. 

When asked whether he would pardon Clancy, Trump called the situation "very sad" but said the case is ultimately a "state situation," not a federal one.

"There’s no winner there. There’s no win no matter what you do. Three children are dead," he said. 

The response came after attorney Kevin Reddington, who represents Clancy, publicly asked Trump to grant his client a pardon last week.

LINDSAY CLANCY'S LAWYER REVEALS POST-MISTRIAL STRATEGY AS RETRIAL LOOMS

Trump indicated that the defense and prosecution need to resolve the legal matter at the local level while praising Reddington's work. 

"He’s a good attorney. I’ve heard from other people he’s a very good attorney," Trump said. "I hope they can work it out. That’s something they have to work out … There is no win there."

Clancy, a 36-year-old former nurse, faces three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of her children: 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan. 

After their deaths, she attempted to kill herself and was paralyzed from the injuries.

item.title: Joanna Gaines reveals why she and Chip walked away from 'Fixer Upper' at the height of its success
item.description: Joanna Gaines described a deep "soul weariness" that led her and Chip Gaines to walk away from "Fixer Upper" despite pressure to keep going.
item.content:encoded:
Joanna Gaines had success knocking on every door — and she decided to stop answering.

At the height of "Fixer Upper" fame, the home design and lifestyle expert and her husband, Chip Gaines, walked away from the nonstop grind despite pressure from their representatives to keep going.

Years later, Joanna explained that she had reached a point where she was experiencing what she called "soul weariness."

JOANNA GAINES KEEPS LIFE SIMPLE IN TEXAS AWAY FROM HOLLYWOOD SPOTLIGHT

"When you start realizing you're living on a thing that's now… the intentionality is gone, and you're just showing up… that doesn't feel fulfilling," she said on the "Joy 101 with Hoda Kotb" podcast. "It actually feels as though we're part of this machine that is like, 'What's the life here?'"

She added, "I would say that was our first pause of like, ‘We're doing all this and seeing great reward … this is wonderful,’ but also never at the expense of … our like livelihood, our happiness, our souls."

That pause would become a blueprint for how Joanna thinks about work — and burnout — today.

"Stopping in that moment was basically us saying … ‘What's worth it is, like are we healthy? Are we good? Is our family good?’ That's the most important thing. So that was really a very pivotal moment for us."

"Fixer Upper" turned Chip and Joanna into television stars, but even as the HGTV hit reached new heights, the couple knew they couldn't keep running at full speed forever.

The Gaines’s first stepped in front of television cameras when the "Fixer Upper" pilot aired in 2013. The series followed the husband-and-wife duo as they took on rundown homes in Waco, Texas, and transformed them into polished spaces for their clients — all while growing their increasingly influential Magnolia brand.

The show quickly became a hit, making Joanna and Chip familiar faces far beyond the world of home renovation.

COUNTRY STAR STEPS AWAY FROM MUSIC TO FOCUS ON HIMSELF AFTER FAME TOOK A TOLL

In September 2017, the couple announced they would end "Fixer Upper" after its fifth season, choosing to step away while the series was still riding high.

Joanna said she and Chip have spent almost 25 years building their business. But about three years ago, she said, they stopped seeing where they were headed.

"We stopped seeing vision. We stopped remembering, ‘Like why are we doing this?’"

The couple decided to take the summer off.

KATHIE LEE GIFFORD ADMITS SHE 'WANTED TO DIE' AFTER MISDIAGNOSIS AND MULTIPLE SURGERIES FOR CHRONIC PAIN

However, the decision wasn't consequence-free. 

Joanna acknowledged that stepping away meant putting pressure on their team.

"Which meant disappointing our team, disappointing a lot of things … So it cost us something. It cost people something."

"But that three months was time for us to go, ‘We need a break. We need clarity. Why are we building this? What are we doing this for?’"

Joanna remembered the moment she felt the burnout was impossible to ignore.

"When you start dreading your days, like ‘I don't want to do that.’"

For Gaines, that sense of dread eventually became so pronounced that she found herself looking for almost any excuse to hit pause — even an unexpected illness.

"You start like wishing for a stomach bug or … 'Okay, maybe back surgery this year would be great.’ Like how do I force myself?" she laughed.

'80S POP STAR TIFFANY EMBRACES QUIET NASHVILLE ROUTINE AFTER LEAVING CALIFORNIA BEHIND FOR GOOD

Physical exhaustion, Joanna explained, is something she knows how to push through.

But the deeper exhaustion is different, she argued.

"So there's that part, but also just … where your soul just feels weary."

She described the "soul" as the deeper part of a person — the place that can run dry even when the body is still capable of performing.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"From a physical standpoint, I can work till I can … I can push past the weariness the physical, but then you get to that layer of like the soul weariness and that's dangerous."

Joanna said that was the warning she is now determined not to ignore, describing the feeling as a "holy fear."

For the entrepreneur and television personality who built an empire by constantly creating, the hardest lesson may have been learning that she cannot simply outwork exhaustion.

The Magnolia Network stars tied the knot in 2003. Joanna and Chip are parents to five children — Ella, Drake, Crew, Emmie and Duke.

As the Gaines’s planted their roots in Waco, Texas, their Magnolia businesses took off.

After five seasons of "Fixer Upper," the original series ended in 2018. Magnolia Network programming later debuted on Discovery+ in 2021 before the linear Magnolia Network replaced DIY Network in January 2022.

The couple's Magnolia Market at the Silos in Waco includes Magnolia Market, the Shops at the Silos, Silos Baking Co. and Magnolia Press Coffee Co. They also operate Magnolia Table elsewhere in Waco.

The design duo additionally publish "Magnolia Journal" and have written a series of lifestyle books. They have a Magnolia Home furniture and accessories collection, and Joanna created the Hearth & Hand with Magnolia collection for Target.

Chip and Joanna also opened the 33-room Hotel 1928 in Waco in 2023 after renovating a historic building in partnership with AJ Capital. The couple also offers Magnolia vacation rentals in Waco.

item.title: Homan confirms 'criminal' investigation involving Ilhan Omar, says he knows 'things are going on’
item.description: Tom Homan confirmed officials are investigating allegations involving Rep. Ilhan Omar but declined to share specifics about possible immigration fraud.
item.content:encoded:
White House border czar Tom Homan confirmed on "The Sunday Briefing" that the Department of Homeland Security is looking into allegations involving Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., but would not disclose details about what he described as an "ongoing criminal investigation."

Pressed on whether the federal government has evidence that Omar committed immigration or naturalization fraud, Homan declined to comment.

"I know things are going on, but I can't give specifics of what's happening," Homan said.

"If someone committed an immigration violation, if someone committed marriage fraud or anything like that, regardless if they're a congressman or not, no one's above the law. So, I'll leave it at that. We'll let HSI, Homeland Security Investigations, continue the investigation."

FEDS SAY RAPE CONVICT LIED HIS WAY INTO US CITIZENSHIP BY HIDING SEX ASSAULTS

When subsequently asked directly whether he was confirming an investigation involving Omar, Homan replied, "I'm confirming that ICE is, yeah — look, I said months ago that there's something that's been reported and needs to be looked at."

Omar has long been dogged by allegations that she married a man that critics allege is her brother as part of an immigration scheme. Omar has repeatedly denied the allegation, and the claim has not been proven in public records. In December, she dismissed the claims as "bigoted lies," writing on social media that Trump was obsessed with her.

Homan's comments follow Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin's appearance on a podcast, during which he said, "Something's going to happen. ... We know that she married her brother to try to bring him to the United States. We know he now lives in London.

ILHAN OMAR LASHES OUT AT 'SICK' REPUBLICANS FOR INVESTIGATING HER ALLEGED MARRIAGE TO BROTHER

"There may be more to this, the whole family migration and possibly some illegal activity for them to come to the United States to begin with. ... If we can prove it, that you shouldn't have been here in the first place, we will deport you."

Homan did not disclose any information about possible evidence or charges.

'SQUAD' DEM DISMISSES FRAUD PROBE SPECULATION AFTER $29M NET-WORTH DROP

Vice President JD Vance said in May that the Justice Department was looking into whether Omar committed immigration fraud.

"You read the things about Ilhan Omar … who she married and whether she didn't marry this person or that person," Vance said then. "It certainly seems like something fishy is there, but everybody's entitled to equal justice under the law."

The vice president's comments follow his own podcast interview in March, during which he told conservative commentator Benny Johnson he had spoken with White House immigration advisor Stephen Miller about potential legal action against Omar.

"We think Ilhan Omar definitely committed immigration fraud against the United States of America," Vance said at the time.

There is a denaturalization process for cases of proven immigration fraud, Homan said, characterizing it as "very serious."

"If someone lies through that process to becoming a citizen, and we can prove they, in fact, lied or misrepresented themselves, we can absolutely denaturalize them. We've done it before many times over the last 40 years I've been around, so it's a process," he said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Omar's office for comment.

Fox News Digital's Louis Casiano contributed to this report.

item.title: Breanna Stewart's double-double, Caitlin Clark's emergence off bench help US to World Cup win over France
item.description: Team USA won its fifth consecutive FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup tournament on Sunday with a dominating victory against France in Germany.
item.content:encoded:
Team USA women’s basketball remained dominant on the world stage on Sunday.

Breanna Stewart, Jackie Young and Caitlin Clark’s emergence off the bench propelled the Americans to a gold-medal victory over France, 97-79. It is Team USA’s fifth consecutive gold medal in the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup and seventh in the last eight tournaments.

The U.S. had to fight and claw its way back into the game after trailing in the first half. But they outscored France 30-12 in the third quarter and used the run to help solidify the victory.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Stewart had a double-double to finish off the French. She scored 22 points and grabbed 10 rebounds. The New York Liberty star’s presence on the interior proved to be a game-changer. She was plus-8 on the floor and shot 70% from the field. She was named MVP of the tournament.

Jackie Young added 18 points, six rebounds and five assists. Young was plus-15 on the floor and shot 50% from the field. She was named the player of the game.

Clark played about 12 minutes off the bench but provided some key buckets for the Americans. She made a buzzer-beating shot before halftime to cut the deficit to two points. As the U.S. continued to surge into the fourth quarter, Clark hit a big 3-pointer to put France on its heels.

She finished with 12 points and three assists.

Though Clark wasn’t a starter in the USA lineup, her presence on the floor in key moments of the game appeared to be fruitful. While the starters needed a breather after getting back into the game, Clark and the rest of her teammates off the bench helped provide the necessary scoring to keep France at bay.

France started out hot.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The duo of Dominique Malonga and Gabby Williams proved to be a formidable force for the Americans to deal with. Malonga scored 21 points to lead France, while Williams added 20 of her own. France didn’t get any other player into double figures. Valeriane Ayayi was the closest as she scored eight points in 26 minutes.

France only made four field goals in the third quarter and the cold streak allowed the U.S. to take the lead and pull away from there.

It is now 12 gold medals in total for the U.S. as they have remained dominant no matter which global tournament they enter.

France may have been the biggest challenge to the U.S. reign as they only lost by one to them in the gold medal game at the 2024 Summer Olympics. But the emergence of young stars like Clark, Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese helped keep the Americans at the top of the food chain throughout the tournament.

The players will take a moment to celebrate the achievement but in a few days, it’s back to the WNBA where the playoffs are on the horizon.

item.title: Nick Saban wants a different criteria for judging which teams reach the College Football Playoff
item.description: Nick Saban urged a strength of schedule overhaul on "College GameDay" before Oregon's shocking upset and Texas' fourth quarter comeback over Ohio State.
item.content:encoded:
If you thought Week 1 of the college football season was wild, Week 2 took the typical chaos to a whole new level.

Out of nowhere, the Oregon Ducks suffered a shocking upset on the road to the recently hapless Oklahoma State Cowboys. The Michigan Wolverines, who dropped out of the Top 25 after a disappointing "win" over Western Michigan, and seemed eliminated from contention for the College Football Playoff, beat the No. 11 Oklahoma Sooners.

The game of the week delivered, in spades, with the Texas Longhorns completing a remarkable fourth quarter comeback at home against the Ohio State Buckeyes. The Buckeyes dominated the game for 45 minutes, had opportunity after opportunity to put the Longhorns away, and missed all of them.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S CHAOS ERA IS HERE: TEXAS RALLIES, OREGON FALLS AND LANE KIFFIN EYES RETURN TO OLE MISS

Even Texas Tech, which seemed set up to run through an easy schedule, struggled on the road against Oregon State before pulling away late in the fourth quarter.

Mostly, the week served as a reminder of what makes college football great: big-name teams playing other big-name teams in incredible environments at historic stadiums. The inherently lesser talent at the collegiate level making come-from-behind wins more possible. And stakes, with wins and losses that matter.

It was also a reminder that in the era of the expanded College Football Playoff, these games are becoming less and less common. Because of misplaced incentives, the rise of superconferences, and a selection committee whose criteria for picking teams are nebulous and ever-shifting at best, and bewildering and incomprehensible at worst.

Legendary head coach Nick Saban, speaking on ESPN's "College GameDay" on Saturday, had some suggestions on how to improve the playoff process and encourage more of these matchups: strength of schedule.

"Players love to play in big games," Saban said. "That’s what great competitors love to do. Fans love to see big games."

"I think what we’ve created now is a system of how many games you win helps you get into playoffs, and the playoffs become the barometer for the success of your program," he continued. "We need a better metric to actually evaluate quality wins and quality losses. Some losses are better than some wins."

That's become a familiar suggestion, particularly from SEC supporters as it moves to nine conference games, guaranteeing an additional eight losses per season spread around the conference. It also makes some obvious sense. Of course, Ohio State shouldn't be punished much for losing to Texas, and that result should carry more weight than a win over Youngstown State.

But this mentality is an accidental argument for the type of evaluation that was used in the BCS era, which fans and many coaches eventually hated. Humans have subjective biases or preferences, and they incorporate those biases and preferences into their rankings. Efficiency-driven rankings do have subjective opinions baked into their underlying model assumptions, but that's less subject to on-field, "eye test" bias than poll rankings.

Still, a blend of success rate and efficiency-based computer-driven rankings and strength-of-resume results might create exactly the system Saban wants. Though it might not create the results he expects.

The 2025 Alabama season is an ideal example. They weren't punished for a blowout loss to the Georgia Bulldogs in the SEC Championship Game. Though they should have been. Not just because of the outcome, but because of how it happened, particularly considering their full season resume.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

After their blowout playoff loss, the Crimson Tide ranked 20th in SP+, an efficiency ranking that doesn't care if you win or lose, it cares how you play, adjusted for the competition you're playing against. Their strength of resume was 19th. They weren't a playoff team, considering their performance against their schedule. Would Saban still be happy with the rankings if it hurts his former team?

The result of this year's Texas-Ohio State game is another fantastic example. By postgame win expectancy, the game was effectively a draw. Texas had a 50.2% win expectancy, with an adjusted scoring margin of 0.0. The teams were nearly identical. In SP+, Ohio State ranks second; Texas ranks sixth, even after the win. Ohio State is still expected to be the better team moving forward, based on how the two have played.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

But if the Buckeyes rank ahead of the Longhorns in human polls, fans, and Saban, will go ballistic.

This is the problem with demanding schedule-driven rankings. Because schedules themselves are subjective, what you value and how you value it, is also subjective. Especially in the NIL/transfer portal era. Fans and voters rank programs based on perception, results in 2025, and brand name, even though it's easier than it's ever been to change your roster and improve overnight. Just look at where Texas Tech is now compared to, say, 2023-2024.

A larger playoff field might also encourage more big games, with teams less "scared" of losing and potentially knocking themselves out. Though few want a 24-team playoff. How does that factor in?

Saban though, did make another, less "controversial" point.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

"And it makes you better as a player," he said about playing other top teams. "Great competition makes you better."

Impossible to argue with that.

item.title: Charlie Kirk statue defaced with red paint, Jesus crossed out days after 1-year mark of assassination
item.description: Red paint was smeared across the Charlie Kirk statue at Turning Point USA's Phoenix headquarters, with a Christian tribute defaced days after unveiling.
item.content:encoded:
Vandals smeared bright red paint across a newly unveiled statue of Charlie Kirk and defaced a Christian tribute outside Turning Point USA’s Phoenix headquarters early Sunday, just three days after the memorial was installed.

Images from the headquarters show red paint streaked across the eight-foot statue’s face and neck, with a crude frowning face drawn across its chest.

A sign at the base of the statue bearing Kirk’s image and the words "Jesus defeated death so you can live" was also targeted. The word "Jesus" and an image of a cross appeared to be crossed out, while "Satan" was apparently scrawled across the display.

REMEMBERING CHARLIE KIRK: TURNING POINT USA'S ANDREW KOLVET REFLECTS ON CONSERVATIVE GROUP'S CHALLENGING YEAR

Kirk's widow, Erika, who now serves as Turning Point USA CEO, responded with a defiant vow to rebuild, saying the vandals would not erase her husband’s legacy or silence Christians. 

"Charlie once said we should be building two statues for every statue that they tear down," Erika Kirk wrote, adding that her husband’s instinct was always to create rather than destroy.

She said the bullet that killed her husband only amplified his voice and predicted the spray paint would spread his legacy even further. She also vowed to restore the statue, replace Jesus Christ’s name on the damaged sign and continue the movement her husband built.

"God will not be mocked," Erika Kirk wrote.

Phoenix police confirmed to Fox News Digital that the department began receiving calls around 8:09 a.m. reporting vandalism to a memorial in the area of 4900 East Beverly Road.

"Officers have responded to the location, and the incident is under investigation," police said.

No arrests or suspect descriptions had been announced as of Sunday afternoon.

"This morning we woke up to radical criminals vandalizing our headquarters," Turning Point USA Chief Operating Officer Tyler Bowyer wrote on social media. "Crossing over Charlie’s face, scratching out Jesus and the Cross and spraying red paint on his neck.

"This isn’t the country we want to live in," Bowyer added. "Arizona is not Gotham."

INSIDE CHARLIE KIRK’S EFFORT TO DEVELOP THE NEXT GENERATION OF CONSERVATIVE VOICES

Bowyer, who went to the headquarters as police investigated, said TPUSA was prepared to clean the memorial as soon as authorities released the scene.

"God bless the police as they investigate the violent thugs who did this," Bowyer wrote.

TPUSA also released video showing the damage and encouraged its supporters to vote ahead of the midterm elections.

"Hate cannot win," the organization wrote. "The radical Left is showing up to vote. What are you doing to save the country from this?"

In a follow-up statement, TPUSA said it would restore the statue and replace the damaged signs while reviewing footage of the incident and working with law enforcement to identify those responsible.

"Vandalism like this is not funny, it’s diabolical," the organization wrote. "The incident happened in the middle of the night because evil never sleeps."

TPUSA said the vandals went beyond spraying Kirk’s face and neck with red paint, accusing them of making an "intentional decision" to cross out Jesus’ name on the nearby sign.

The organization ended its response by quoting John 15:18: "If the world hates you, keep in mind that it hated me first."

The vandalism struck only days after TPUSA unveiled the bronze statue Thursday to mark one year since Kirk was assassinated while speaking at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025.

CHARLIE KIRK STATUE BOUND FOR NY'S TIMES SQUARE AS SCULPTOR DEFIES THREATS AHEAD OF UNVEILING

The statue depicts Kirk wearing his signature "Freedom" T-shirt and cross necklace. Those who knew him said the sculpture captured details down to his wedding ring, according to FOX 10 Phoenix.

Turning Point USA commissioned Utah artist Quintin McCann to create the memorial after he began working on a portrait of Kirk the evening the conservative activist was killed, according to the outlet.

ITALIAN ARTIST UNVEILS CHARLIE KIRK MEMORIAL STATUE HE PLANS TO FEATURE AT TIMES SQUARE

"Someone’s death, who I’ve never met, has never impacted me so much," McCann told FOX 10. "And I’m sure many people can agree. And I just stayed at work that evening and just started sculpting his portrait."

The statue was initially placed outside TPUSA’s headquarters near 48th Street and Beverly Road but was expected to be moved indoors for security reasons by the end of the week, the outlet reported.

REPUBLICAN CONVENTION ATTENDEES SHARE HEARTFELT TRIBUTES TO LATE CHARLIE KIRK ON ASSASSINATION ANNIVERSARY

Conservative voices erupted over the attack, condemning the vandalism as another assault on Kirk’s family, friends and legacy.

"Truly abhorrent," Rep. Abe Hamadeh, R-Ariz., wrote on X. "The Charlie Kirk statue that was just unveiled at Turning Point’s HQ was vandalized overnight with red paint.

"The young people who work at Turning Point don’t deserve this, Charlie’s family doesn’t deserve this, his friends don’t deserve this," Hamadeh added. "The left is intolerant and militant. Evil exists and must be confronted continuously."

Rep. Andy Biggs, R-Ariz., was equally blunt.

"This is absolute evil," Biggs wrote.

Conservative commentator Benny Johnson accused the vandals of trying to intimidate Kirk’s supporters.

"These people are incapable of building anything, all they know is destruction," Johnson wrote. "Keep these demons out of power."

TPUSA contributor Alex Clark said seeing the damage brought her to tears before issuing a dire warning to conservative voters.

"The left wants to tap dance in your blood and throw confetti at your gravestone," Clark wrote. "Vote red in midterms like your life depends on it because it actually does as a conservative."

Turning Point USA Chief of Staff Mikey McCoy urged conservatives to answer the vandalism with faith, invoking Kirk’s willingness to return to hostile campuses and the biblical examples of Stephen and Christ praying for those who persecuted them.

"Then I can surrender all the anger, and pure disgust that I feel at seeing this to a just and holy God," McCoy wrote, saying he would pray instead for the repentance and salvation of those responsible.

"Lord, help our Country," he added. "Open their eyes. Break their hearts. Save them."

Bowyer also blasted Democratic Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs, accusing her of failing to pursue bipartisanship after Kirk’s killing and pointing to her veto of legislation that would have named Loop 202 in Kirk’s honor.

Hobbs said in her March veto letter that she condemned political violence but argued highway-naming decisions should remain nonpartisan and be handled by the state board responsible for such designations.

Kirk was 31 when he was shot and killed during a TPUSA event at Utah Valley University. 

Tyler Robinson, 23, has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder and other charges in Kirk’s death. Prosecutors are seeking the death penalty.

Erika Kirk took over as CEO of Turning Point USA after her husband’s assassination. The conservative organization he co-founded in 2012 has continued expanding its network of high school and college chapters since his death.

Anyone with information about the vandalism is asked to contact Phoenix police or Silent Witness at 480-WITNESS.

Fox News Digital has reached out to Turning Point USA and Hobbs’ office for additional information and comment.

item.title: Saints defense has touchdown taken away against Lions after Jared Goff fumble is stunningly overturned
item.description: Chase Young forced what looked like a Jared Goff fumble, but officials ruled it an incomplete pass, wiping a New Orleans Saints defensive touchdown.
item.content:encoded:
The New Orleans Saints scored a routine defensive touchdown against the Detroit Lions on Sunday afternoon. Or so they thought, or so everyone thought.

With the Lions on top 7-0 early in the second quarter, New Orleans defensive end Chase Young beat his man on the edge and forced what looked to be a routine fumble out of Detroit quarterback Jared Goff. It appeared to be a straightforward fumble given that the ball traveled backward, and Goff's arm did not look to be moving forward.

Saints safety Jonas Sanker ultimately picked up the football and carried it into the end zone untouched to get New Orleans on the scoreboard, but only for a brief moment.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

After reviewing the play, officials determined that Goff had started his throwing motion, and given that the quarterback's intent was to throw the football forward, it was ruled an incomplete pass.

ZAC TAYLOR ADMITS BREAKING NFL CHALLENGE FLAG RULE FOR 8 YEARS AS LEAGUE MAKES CHANGE

The football didn't actually travel forward, but Goff's intention overrules the fact that the ball traveled backward, apparently.

"He had started his throwing motion," Mike Pereira, NFL rules analyst for Fox Sports, explained on the broadcast. "Now, throwing motion is bringing the ball up; forget about the hand at this point going forward. Throwing motion starts, hand going up, then he's hit, ball comes loose, his intent was to throw it forward. Since that motion had already started, that's going to be an incomplete pass, no matter where it lands."

While taking intent into consideration feels like a gray area, especially during a bang-bang play, the explanation that it doesn't matter where the football actually lands makes the rule that much more confusing.

Nevertheless, the Saints' touchdown was wiped off the board, the Lions ultimately punted at the end of the drive, and Detroit took a 7-0 lead into halftime.

We're not even a full week into the 2026 NFL season, but the Goff fumble being reversed because of his intent to throw the football forward could go down as the strangest sequence of the year.

item.title: Meghan Markle shares intimate first glimpse of life in UK since surprising move
item.description: Meghan Markle's Instagram video shows Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet enjoying the English countryside weeks after the family's UK return.
item.content:encoded:

item.content:encoded:
Former Arizona Sen. Kyrsten Sinema questioned whether there is still room for moderates in the Democratic Party, saying it was made "clear" they didn’t want her there before she abandoned her Democratic affiliation and became an independent. 

"The reason I left was because the party had decided they wanted to pursue a track of short-term gain and really sacrificing kind of longer-term issues around democracy, like the filibuster," she said Saturday on "My View with Lara Trump." 

"And they very much made it clear that they didn't really want me there. And, so, I left, which made me happy, and I think made them happy.

"But I'm not sure that there's more room for others who are moderate or conservatives left there. ... That's unfortunate because the majority of Americans actually live in that moderate or fiscally conservative middle." 

SHOCKING PERCENTAGE OF DEMOCRATS IDENTIFY AS 'DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS' ACCORDING TO NEW POLL: 'TOXIC POLICIES'

Sinema, who was elected to both the House and Senate as a Democrat before becoming an independent, said she left the party after Democrats pursued what she characterized as immediate political gains at the expense of longer-term institutional concerns, specifically citing the filibuster.

WISCONSIN DEMOCRATIC CANDIDATE SAYS HER PARTY 'LEFT BEHIND' RURAL AMERICA

Sinema said when she entered Congress in 2012, she was a "blue dog," a coalition she described as fiscally conservative and socially moderate. There were a lot more traditional liberal Democrats at that time, she said, stating that the DSA is something else entirely.

"It's really rooted in tenets of socialism, which is not reflective of the historic Democratic Party. So, it's hard to tell whether it's a hijacking or whether it is actually the movement of the voters' opinions," she said.

item.title: Thousands of hacked sites trick you into installing malware
item.description: Over 5,400 legitimate websites now serve fake CAPTCHA scams that trick users into pasting malware commands into Windows Run via ClickFix attacks.
item.content:encoded:
You land on the real website of a local business and a CAPTCHA appears. It looks routine until the page tells you to open Windows Run and paste a command. That should stop you cold.

Security researchers say thousands of legitimate small-business websites have been compromised to spread this malware trap. Here's what to know before a familiar website catches you off guard.

FAKE PATIENT PORTAL SCAM CAN STEAL YOUR LOGIN AND INFECT YOUR PC

This campaign is much bigger than a handful of infected pages. Netskope Threat Labs says it identified more than 5,400 compromised websites across more than 2,200 organizations worldwide over the past few months.

The sites have little in common beyond many belonging to small businesses. Researchers found clinics, plumbing companies, online stores and other businesses among the victims.

Where Netskope examined individual sites, they most often ran WordPress and sometimes PrestaShop. Researchers still do not know how attackers initially compromised them.

That is important because you could visit the legitimate website of a business you recognize and still encounter a malicious prompt.

Netskope says several hundred compromised sites can be active on a given day. It has recently seen more than 300 sites contacting the malicious infrastructure each weekday.

The attack starts with malicious code hidden inside a compromised website. When you visit the site, that code can load another script. Then the page may blur and show what looks like an ordinary CAPTCHA.

Instead of simply asking you to prove you are human, the page tells you to open the Windows Run dialog and paste a command. That command can download and launch the attacker's malware.

Here is the warning sign I want you to remember: A legitimate CAPTCHA should never tell you to open Windows Run or paste a command into your computer.

We have seen fake CAPTCHA scams use this same trick before. The page looks familiar, so you may assume the instructions are part of a normal security check. They are not. The criminal is trying to get you to launch the attack yourself.

CLICKLOCK MAC MALWARE LOCKS APPS UNTIL YOU GIVE IN

This technique is known as ClickFix. The clever part has less to do with some exotic computer hack and more to do with psychology.

You are already used to CAPTCHAs. Websites ask you to click a box or prove you are human all the time. So, when a convincing verification screen appears on a legitimate website, your guard may be down. Then the instructions make the dangerous action look like one more step in the verification process.

Cybercriminals have used similar ClickFix tricks with fake Windows update screens. The appearance changes, but the warning remains the same. A webpage should not be telling you to run computer commands.

This is where the campaign gets more unusual. The attackers are using the BNB Smart Chain test network to store instructions used by the compromised websites.

You do not need to understand cryptocurrency to understand why criminals like this setup. Normally, attackers might keep malicious code on a regular web server. Once investigators find that server, a hosting provider may be able to shut it down.

A blockchain works differently. In this campaign, the attackers store code inside something called a smart contract. Think of it as a place where the hacked websites can check for their next set of instructions.

Netskope says the attackers are using the test version of BNB Smart Chain. Developers normally use this network to experiment without spending real cryptocurrency.

That gives the criminals inexpensive infrastructure that can also be harder to take down through traditional methods. There is another advantage.

The attacker can change what the smart contract delivers. The compromised websites can then pick up those new instructions without criminals having to modify every hacked site individually. That helps explain why this infrastructure is so useful to them.

Netskope also found a newer version of the attack that skips the fake CAPTCHA. This version uses technology called WebRTC. Your browser normally uses WebRTC for things such as video calls and real-time communications. The attackers found another use for it.

Their code can create an encrypted data connection with the attacker and receive additional malicious code through the browser. Netskope says the code can then run without first being saved as a traditional file on the computer.

For you, the technical details are less important than the larger point. The criminals can change how the attack works while continuing to use the same network of compromised websites.

A few simple habits can help you avoid handing control of your computer to an attacker.

If a website tells you to open Windows Run, PowerShell or Command Prompt, stop. Do not paste anything it gives you. Close the page instead.

A normal CAPTCHA may ask you to click a checkbox or identify pictures. It should not require you to change settings or run commands on your PC. If the instructions suddenly leave the browser, close the page.

Strong antivirus protection can help detect malicious scripts and malware if something slips past you. Keep it updated and enable real-time protection. If you accidentally follow suspicious instructions, run a full system scan. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android & iOS devices at Cyberguy.com

Install security updates when they become available. However, update Windows through Windows Update. Update your browser through its built-in settings or official source. Do not trust an unexpected webpage that says you must download an update.

If you followed the instructions from a suspicious CAPTCHA, disconnect the computer from the internet. Run a full antivirus scan. Then use another trusted device to change passwords for sensitive accounts you accessed on that computer. Start with your main email account. Also review active login sessions and enable multifactor authentication wherever you can.

Website owners should take this campaign seriously too. Netskope recommends checking the integrity of your content management system files. Researchers found malicious code added to legitimate JavaScript files or hidden inside fake plugin directories. Keep WordPress, PrestaShop and any plugins you use updated. Remove plugins you no longer need. Keep in mind that Netskope has not identified how attackers initially broke into the websites in this campaign. Those steps are good security practices, but researchers have not tied a specific WordPress or PrestaShop vulnerability to these compromises.

What gets me about this attack is how ordinary everything can look at first. You could be visiting the real website of a neighborhood business you have used before. Then a familiar CAPTCHA appears. That sense of trust is exactly what can make the next instruction dangerous. The blockchain technology behind the campaign makes life harder for security teams trying to shut it down. For the rest of us, though, the best defense is refreshingly simple. A website should never need you to open Windows Run or paste a command to prove you are human. If you see that request, close the page. That one warning sign could save you from installing malware yourself.

Would you recognize a fake CAPTCHA if it appeared on the website of a business you already trusted, or would the familiar site make you more likely to follow the instructions? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

item.title: Arrest rips apart media narrative on death of Black woman found hanging from Mississippi tree
item.description: Jarques Ratliff faces a murder charge in the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old mother found hanging from a tree behind a Jackson, Mississippi home.
item.content:encoded:
Mississippi authorities have arrested a 51-year-old man on a murder charge after an official homicide ruling in the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old Black mother of four found hanging from a tree behind an abandoned home last month.

The arrest follows weeks of intense media attention and widespread online discussion regarding the circumstances surrounding Fortune’s death in a state with a historic legacy of racialized violence. But law enforcement officials confirmed that the suspect taken into custody is Jarques Ratliff, a Black Jackson resident who had a prior personal connection with Fortune.

Jackson Police Chief RaShall Brackney announced during a news conference Saturday that Ratliff was taken into custody without incident while walking along Capitol Street in Jackson, shortly after officers executed search warrants at related properties. 

AOC’S ‘MODERN-DAY LYNCHINGS’ CLAIM TORN TO SHREDS ONLINE AS BLACK HANGING CASE FINDINGS TELL A DIFFERENT STORY

Chief Brackney emphasized that while the arrest marks a significant breakthrough, the investigation remains active and additional arrest warrants are expected to be served as detectives follow further leads.

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., last week warned of "racial terror" and "widespread modern-day lynchings" in the U.S. as she joined dozens of Democrats demanding that the Department of Justice investigate hanging deaths of Black Americans.

Fortune’s body was discovered Aug. 3 in the backyard of a vacant property in the 500 block of Road of Remembrance in Jackson. 

Although investigators logged hundreds of hours interviewing nearly 15 individuals and reviewing physical evidence over the past month, formal arrest warrants could not be executed until the Mississippi State Medical Examiner’s Office officially classified Fortune’s death a homicide late Thursday. 

Once that classification was handed down, members of the Jackson Police Department's robbery-homicide unit moved swiftly to secure and execute two search warrants alongside the arrest warrant for Ratliff.

Addressing public interest in the case, Chief Brackney acknowledged the heightened scrutiny but stressed that law enforcement remains strictly guided by verifiable physical evidence rather than external speculation. She noted that authorities understood public concern given Mississippi's history but said the department is bound to ensure all public statements are backed by forensic facts.

"We understand that this case has received media attention from across the globe and across the community. We understand the questions and the desire for answers given Mississippi's history," Brackney said. 

"We understand this case is being viewed through a broader lens — a global lens — and we do not dismiss those concerns. We are taking them seriously. At the same time, we do have a responsibility to make sure that what we say publicly is supported by our evidence and the facts."

Brackney also directly clarified that law enforcement had never officially designated any persons of interest prior to Ratliff’s arrest, refuting social media reports that a 65-year-old man had previously been identified as a suspect.

COPS DROP MURDER PROBE AFTER CORONER RULES MAN’S BLOODY STABBING DEATH WAS FREAK ACCIDENT

Fortune's mother, Christy Spivey, said police promptly notified her family of the homicide ruling and Ratliff's arrest on Friday. Spivey expressed gratitude for the police work and reiterated her firm belief that her daughter did not die by suicide, adding that Fortune would never take her own life.

According to family members and an online obituary published in Kentucky, Fortune grew up in Kentucky, skipped her junior year of high school and was a star cross-country runner guided by strong religious faith before relocating to Jackson a decade ago. 

Spivey noted that her daughter had experienced homelessness in recent years but was actively working to launch a cleaning business and stabilize her life prior to her death.

Ratliff is being held at the Hinds County Detention Center on a charge of murder. According to Mississippi State Defender André de Gruy, Ratliff is scheduled to make his initial appearance in Jackson Municipal Court no later than Monday morning, where formal charges will be read and bond conditions set. 

Police have not publicly detailed the specific physical evidence linking Ratliff to the scene, nor have they expanded on the exact nature of his personal association with Fortune as investigators prepare for further potential arrests.

President Donald Trump has a blunt message for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as Kyiv continues targeting Russia: Stop hitting its diesel refineries.

Trump made the remarks Sunday while attending the Irish Open at his golf club in Doonbeg, Ireland, after a reporter asked whether he had spoken with Zelenskyy following a recent conversation with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"Zelensky has to do one thing. He has to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia," Trump told reporters.

TRUMP NEGOTIATORS WITKOFF, KUSHNER MEET WITH PUTIN IN MOSCOW AS US PUSHES FOR END TO RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR

Trump said Ukraine could continue pursuing other targets inside Russia but urged Zelenskyy to steer clear of the country’s diesel infrastructure.

"Let him go after targets, but not diesel fuel because he's causing a shortage of diesel," Trump said. "This isn't done by the Middle East. This is done by what's happening with Russia and Ukraine."

The president said he had already spoken directly with Zelenskyy about the issue.

"So we spoke to Mr. Zelensky about it. There are plenty of other targets," Trump said. "Don't hit diesel fuel because that's hurting the world. We don't want him to hit diesel fuel. He's hitting diesel refineries."

WATCH: FIGHTS BREAK OUT AT RUSSIAN GAS STATIONS AS PUTIN ADMITS FUEL SHORTAGES

Trump’s remarks come as Ukraine has targeted Russia’s oil and gas infrastructure with long-range strikes, part of Kyiv’s effort to hamper an industry that provides revenue and fuel for Moscow’s war effort. Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine more than four years ago.

The strikes have put pressure on Russia’s fuel supplies, prompting rationing in parts of the country and a Russian ban on diesel exports in July. The disruption has also added pressure to global diesel supplies, which have faced additional strain amid reduced oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.

Diesel prices in the U.S. climbed above an average of $6 per gallon on Friday, reaching a record high.

Russia has intensified its aerial attacks on Ukraine in recent weeks, including strikes involving ballistic missiles and drones, while Ukraine has continued targeting sites inside Russia.

Russian and Ukrainian officials reported another round of large-scale drone attacks overnight into Sunday, with casualties reported on both sides.

OBAMA STRATEGIST TURNS ON RISING DEM STAR OVER VIRAL TRUMP ATTACK: 'GRATUITOUS AND UNNECESSARY'

The attention surrounding Harp began after Sen. Ossoff, D-Ga., invoked her by her first name while criticizing Trump during a campaign speech. Conservatives interpreted Ossoff's remarks as insinuating an inappropriate relationship between Trump and Harp, an interpretation Ossoff later rejected.

Ossoff made the reference while accusing Trump of being more interested in personal pursuits than carrying out presidential duties.

"He doesn’t want to do the job. He wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie on their apparently defenseless flying palace gifted by the emir of Qatar," Ossoff said.

HOUSE DEM'S 'LAKE NATALIE' JAB AT TRUMP AIDE SETS SOCIAL MEDIA ABLAZE: 'STAY CLASSY'

Fox News Digital reached out to Rupar, the White House and Ossoff for comment but did not immediately receive responses.

Ossoff later faced questions from MS Now host Jen Psaki about why he specifically named Harp. He denied suggesting an affair and instead said his reference was about the advisors surrounding Trump.

"Well, I've heard this particular aide referred to as his security blanket, and I think we could say that about any number of the senior aides in the White House," Ossoff said.

The White House responded forcefully to Ossoff’s initial remarks, defending Harp as one of Trump’s top aides.

"Natalie Harp is one of the most loyal and hardest working aides on President Trump's team. Jon Ossoff is a cringeworthy, feminine theatre kid cosplaying as Barack Obama. Nobody gives a s--- what this lightweight loser says," White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

In August, Fox News Digital reported that CNN and MS NOW had mentioned Harp hundreds of times in the days after Ossoff's remarks after CNN alone had mentioned her at least 132 times by Aug. 19.

Graham previously told Fox News Digital the coverage of Harp was failing to address what he considered the "fundamental question" about why her routine presence alongside the president had become a major media story.

item.title: Popular GLP-1 weight-loss drugs linked to potentially deadly brain disorder
item.description: A study linked 15 cases of Wernicke encephalopathy to GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic and Mounjaro, raising concerns about vitamin B1 deficiency risks.
item.content:encoded:
Researchers are warning about a rare but potentially life-threatening brain condition that may be linked to popular GLP-1 weight-loss medications.

A new study, published in Clinical Nutrition, identified 15 reported cases of Wernicke encephalopathy, a neurological disorder caused by severe vitamin B1 deficiency, in people taking GLP-1 receptor agonists.

Most of the reported cases involved semaglutide, sold under the brand names Ozempic and Wegovy, or tirzepatide, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound.

DOCTORS REVEAL HIDDEN DANGER FOR SOME OZEMPIC, WEGOVY USERS WITH BRAIN DISORDERS

Researchers found 15 cases through the FDA's Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS), published medical literature and their own medical center.

Most patients reported gastrointestinal symptoms or nutritional issues, including weight loss, vomiting, loss of appetite or malnutrition, the study noted.

Reports of the disorder appeared more often among people taking GLP-1 medications than among those taking other drugs, the researchers found. They emphasized, however, that the study cannot prove the medications caused the condition.

Vitamin B1 plays an important role in brain function, the researchers said. Severe deficiencies can cause confusion, trouble walking, balance problems and vision changes. If left untreated, the condition can lead to permanent neurological damage or death.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Karthik Achari, a Chicago-based clinician and founder of PepMD who was not involved in the study, said the findings should be viewed in perspective.

"Researchers went through adverse event reports and the medical literature and found a small number of cases, 15, of Wernicke encephalopathy in people taking GLP-1 drugs," Achari told Fox News Digital. "That's out of millions of people on these medications. So this is rare."

"But it's real, it's serious, and the mechanism makes sense," he added.

GLP-1 medications can reduce appetite while also causing nausea and vomiting, making it easier for some people to become deficient in vitamin B1, Achari said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"The drug shrinks your appetite. It doesn't shrink your body's requirements," he said. "You can now eat very little without feeling it, which is the point of the medication, but your need for protein, vitamins, and fluids didn't go anywhere."

People with persistent nausea and vomiting, those losing weight very quickly while eating little, people with a history of bariatric surgery and those who use alcohol heavily may face a higher risk, Achari said.

Erin Palinski-Wade, a New Jersey-based nutritionist and author of "The Sleepdemic Solution," said proper nutrition and hydration should be considered part of treatment while taking GLP-1 medications.

"GLP-1 medications can dramatically reduce appetite, but that also means people may unintentionally under-eat the very things their bodies need most, especially protein, fiber and fluids," she told Fox News Digital.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Palinski-Wade said ongoing vomiting or diarrhea can increase the risk of dehydration and kidney problems. She urged patients to seek medical guidance if those symptoms continue for roughly 24 hours.

"Don't assume every side effect is just part of being on a GLP-1," Palinski-Wade said. "Severe or persistent symptoms deserve attention."

The researchers acknowledged that the study relied largely on reports submitted to the FDA and cannot prove GLP-1 medications caused the condition. They called for additional research, and experts said patients should not stop taking prescribed GLP-1 medications based on these findings alone.

Fox News Digital reached out to Novo Nordisk, Eli Lilly and the researchers for comment.

item.title: Cruise passengers erupt over 'rude' luggage habit that sharply divides travelers
item.description: Etiquette expert Diane Gottsman of Texas weighed in on the heated cruise elevator debate about travelers using rolling suitcases on packed disembarkation day mornings.
item.content:encoded:
Cruise passengers are debating a heated topic among vacation travelers who take to the ocean.

Does bringing luggage into crowded ship elevators cross a major etiquette line, especially on hectic disembarkation mornings?

Those carrying their own bags often depend on elevators to move between decks as thousands of passengers prepare to leave the ship. Now, social media posts are fueling a broader argument over whether squeezing suitcases into packed elevators is practical or just plain rude.

OUTRAGED CRUISE PASSENGERS SOUND OFF ABOUT ‘IMMENSE DISAPPOINTMENT’ AFTER ABRUPT CANCELLATION

Diane Gottsman, an etiquette expert based in Texas, said passengers can bring luggage into elevators, though they should be considerate of the limited space.

"When it comes to traveling, space is a priority," Gottsman told Fox News Digital. "You always have to think about the people that are going to be around you."

Gottsman said passengers can leave larger suitcases outside their cabin the night before for crew members to collect.

"When possible, it's always best to keep your suitcases to a minimum when getting on a crowded cruise ship elevator," she said.

MAJOR AIRLINE ROASTS PASSENGERS WHO JUMP UP RIGHT AFTER LANDING, IGNITING FIERCE BACKLASH

Passengers who prefer to carry their own luggage can do so, she added, but should be prepared to manage it themselves.

Cruise lines also have their own procedures for handling bags.

Carnival Cruise Line states on its website that checked baggage service during embarkation ends two hours before a ship's scheduled sailing time.

"Guests arriving after this time will be responsible for taking their bags on board," the cruise line states.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Planning ahead is especially important on busy embarkation and disembarkation days, Gottsman said.

"We know when we're getting off a cruise ship, it's going to be busy," she said. "Everyone is getting off the same cruise ship. So you have to plan in advance."

She advised passengers to let others exit before boarding and wait for another elevator if one is already packed.

"Don't just charge on with your luggage," Gottsman said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Passengers with mobility issues should also be given priority, while those with extra luggage should be prepared to wait, she added.

The issue recently surfaced on Reddit after a first-time cruiser said the traveler and partner were scoffed at by another passenger while taking an elevator from Deck 14 to Deck 5 with their rolling suitcases.

Many cruisers defended the couple — arguing that elevators are often the most practical option for passengers carrying luggage across multiple decks.

"I always hand-roll my luggage off. I always use the elevator," one Reddit user wrote. "I'm not hauling my bags up and down stairs."

Another commenter asked, "How else would you get your luggage down that many decks?"

Said another person, "People find any reason to complain [about] a ship elevator. My mom was on a scooter [due to] her bad back/knees, and people were so rude to her at the elevators."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Yet another person chimed in, "The rudeness always seems higher on disembarkation day. You didn’t do anything wrong. I would only use the stairs if it was a flight or two just to save time, otherwise I would definitely use it."

Other cruisers said bringing luggage into an elevator is fine as long as passengers remain considerate of those around them.

"You can absolutely use the elevators, just be cognizant of others and make space when you can," one commenter wrote.

Some disagreed, arguing that using the ship's luggage service can make departure easier for everyone.

"The whole point of the luggage delivery is to make it easier for everyone," one person wrote.

Cruise industry experts projected a worldwide increase in the number of people taking to the ocean this year — breaking last year’s record, The Associated Press reported several months ago. 

In an April report released by the Cruise Lines International Association, an estimated 38.3 million people were projected to travel on ships this year — a number that's 4% higher than last year’s 37.2 million record-breaking number of passengers.

item.title: Election chaos in this red state just got even stranger for Republicans after Supreme Court ruling
item.description: The Supreme Court blocked Missouri's new congressional map, forcing the state to use 2022 boundaries that favor Emanuel Cleaver's Kansas City district.
item.content:encoded:
Republicans suffered a fresh blow in Missouri after the Supreme Court blocked a congressional map that could have helped the GOP gain another House seat in November.

The ruling, handed down last week, means Missouri will use its 2022 congressional map instead of the new boundaries backed by President Donald Trump and Missouri Republicans.

Missouri held its August primary under the new map, meaning candidates won their party nominations based on one set of district boundaries. But those boundaries will change before the November election, when Missouri is expected to return to its 2022 map.

TRUMP DANGLES $5,000 CHECKS AS DEBT SURGES — BUT ONLY IF GOP CAN CLEAR MAJOR MIDTERM HURDLE

Typically, states redraw their congressional and state legislative districts once every decade after the Census to account for population changes and ensure that each district has roughly the same number of residents.

The new map would have shifted parts of Democratic Rep. Emanuel Cleaver’s Kansas City district into more Republican-leaning areas, making the seat more competitive.

Republicans hoped the changes would help them win seven of Missouri’s eight House seats in the November midterm elections. The GOP currently holds six of the state’s eight seats, while Democrats hold two.

Missouri must now use the 2022 map, which keeps Cleaver’s district more favorable to Democrats.

The Supreme Court’s decision came after more than a year of legal battles over which congressional map Missouri should use.

Missouri held its August primary under the new map, but the state will use its 2022 district boundaries for the November general election. That means some voters could be assigned to a different congressional district in November than the one in which they voted during the primary.

The change could affect more than 1 million voters, or nearly one-fourth of Missouri’s electorate, according to an Associated Press estimate.

The conflicting court orders have added to the confusion, with the November election just weeks away. Candidates and election officials must now adjust to the 2022 boundaries.

MISSOURI HIGH COURT BLOCKS GOP-BACKED CONGRESSIONAL MAPS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS; TRUMP BLASTS 'RIDICULOUS' RULING

The Supreme Court did not explain its reasoning in the brief order.

The White House did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

item.title: FIBA Secretary General Andreas Zagklis speaks out on Caitlin Clark's impact on growth of World Cup
item.description: FIBA's secretary general says Caitlin Clark and women's basketball stars could surpass male players in popularity at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
item.content:encoded:
FIBA Secretary General Andreas Zagklis addressed the impact of Caitlin Clark and other new young players playing in the World Cup for the first time on the tournament's growth and visibility.

Zagklis, speaking at a press conference before the World Cup Final against France, called Clark one of the biggest stars of her generation and predicted that the popularity of the women's basketball players could surpass the men's at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

"I think what these players, Caitlin, one of them, have done in increasing the popularity of the women's game is incredible. We should feel very proud about them. And I can tell you, me and my team have been supportive of what USA Basketball and each and every national member federation coming into the World Cup had planned for their promotion. And we tried to amplify that experience. They themselves, the players said this is a unique moment for them," Zagklis said.

THE PREDOMINANT BASKETBALL DYNASTY ON EARTH IS AT STAKE AS AMERICA'S EYES TURN TO CAITLIN CLARK'S ROLE

"So while I may not be able to quantify the answer and give you exact numbers, but our team perhaps can do that after the tournament, I can tell you that the popularity of our women's game, of Caitlin as one of the biggest stars, not the biggest star of this generation has done. We see this with Iyana Martin from Spain, MVP of the under-19 in 2023. And she signed a big sponsorship agreement herself just with a FIBA partner two days before the tournament.

"So players around the world are picking up these opportunities. And I'm extremely proud of them. And I can tell you, I do believe that in the Los Angeles Olympics, our female players may be at the same or even higher level of popularity than many of our former male players. And this is not a criticism to anybody. It's just a result of the collective growth of the game. And we're proud for both the male and female players that we have to admit have made our sport as global as it is today."

Clark has become one the biggest storylines of this year's tournament, and has done so without even starting a game.

Clark has come off the bench in each of Team USA's five wins, alongside fellow young stars Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers, as coach Kara Lawson has opted to play the veteran starters in all five of the U.S. wins.

Still, Clark has been among the tournament's top performers.

The 24-year-old guard has clocked just over 20 minutes per game, placing her among the team's most utilized players. In those minutes, she has proven to be an elite facilitator, currently ranking third in the entire World Cup with 5.8 assists per game.

Her playmaking was most obvious in the team's opening victory over China, where she immediately accelerated the American offense to the tune of 14 points and a record-setting 11 assists without committing a single turnover.

item.title: Obama privately sounds alarm on ‘dangerous’ AI, urges Democrats to put issue at center of agenda
item.description: Barack Obama warned AI could become dangerous without greater oversight and urged Hakeem Jeffries to launch a very public conversation on it.
item.content:encoded:
Former President Barack Obama urged Democrats during a private fundraiser in New York City Thursday to place artificial intelligence near the center of their political agenda ahead of the midterms and 2028 presidential race while warning that the technology could become dangerous without greater oversight as voters increasingly raise concerns about jobs, privacy and data centers.

Obama, speaking alongside House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., warned party donors and lawmakers that policymakers risk losing control of an industry developing largely in private hands, The New York Times reported.

"This is something that is moving very fast in private hands, and if we don’t get on top of it, I think can be dangerous," Obama said. "If we do get on top of it, I do think it’s beneficial. I genuinely think it’s going to accelerate, for example, drug development in ways that can help us cure diseases. I do think that this can help us figure out pathways for a clean energy future."

RNC member and Humans First Chairwoman Amy Kremer told Fox News Digital Sunday she agreed policymakers need to recognize both AI’s benefits and risks but pushed back on turning greater authority over to the federal government or technology companies.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS SEE AI REGULATION AS URGENT, RANK SAFEGUARDS AHEAD OF INNOVATION

"You don't have to agree on politics to recognize reality: AI is moving incredibly fast, and policymakers need to understand both the opportunities and the very real risks that come with it," Kremer told Fox News Digital. 

"Where I likely disagree with President Obama is on what government should do about it. The answer isn't handing Washington bureaucrats more control, and it certainly isn't allowing Big Tech to write the rules that govern itself.

"We need guardrails that protect Americans while allowing American innovation to lead the world. That means protecting children, workers and our national security, while making sure China doesn't win the AI race."

Obama's warning comes as Fox News Digital polling found substantial voter resistance to the infrastructure powering the AI boom.

A July Fox News poll found 70% of registered voters opposed construction of AI data centers in their communities, compared with 30% who supported them.

MAGA BEGINS TO CRACK AS 2026 GOP ROSTER BACKS AWAY FROM TRUMP'S TECH VISION

The debate has also divided Republicans as data centers become a more prominent midterm issue. Several Republican candidates have called for limits or pauses on new projects despite President Donald Trump's support for expanding data center development.

At the closed-door fundraiser, Obama directly urged Jeffries to prepare Democrats to make AI policy a public issue if the party takes control of the House.

"Once you are speaker, I would strongly urge that the Democrats put together a framework for a very public conversation," Obama said.

Obama also urged prospective 2028 presidential candidates to develop a "very clear plan" for AI and make the technology one of their "central agendas," according to the partial transcript provided by his office to The New York Times. He identified potential job displacement and effects on children among the issues candidates should address.

Public anxiety extends beyond data centers. An April Fox News poll found 63% of voters believed AI hurts privacy, while 56% said it hurts U.S. job creation. Just 21% said the technology helps job creation.

DEMOCRATS SOUND ALARM OVER AI JOB APOCALYPSE — BUT LABOR MARKET ISN'T FOLLOWING SCRIPT

Trump has emphasized rapid AI development and maintaining the United States' competitive position against China. His administration unveiled its first national AI policy framework in March, calling for a consistent national standard while addressing issues including free speech, child safety and energy costs.

"The only reason that communities throughout the U.S.A. should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor," Trump said.

Concerns about AI accelerated again Saturday when Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for slowing the development race, warning that advances could outpace humans' ability to understand and control the systems. Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman subsequently expressed support for Amodei's call.

Jeffries backed Obama’s call for action and sought to draw a contrast with Republicans.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"President Obama is correct that decisive action must be taken on artificial intelligence," Jeffries said. "Republicans have abdicated their responsibility to govern on behalf of the American people. We will not repeat their error."

House Democrats are already developing an AI policy framework that is expected to be released this fall after review by Jeffries, according to The New York Times.

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House and Palantir for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Female passenger undresses on American Airlines flight, engages in 'indecent acts,' crew reports
item.description: A female passenger on American Airlines Flight 1779 reportedly undressed and performed indecent acts mid-flight, prompting law enforcement at Miami.
item.content:encoded:
Law enforcement officers met an American Airlines flight upon its arrival at Miami International Airport late Friday night following reports of a female passenger undressing and behaving indecently mid-flight.

American Airlines Flight 1779 departed Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport (BWI) just after 9 p.m. EDT on Friday, Sept. 11, 2025, nearly two hours behind its scheduled departure time, according to public flight-tracking data. The flight landed in Miami at approximately 11:23 p.m. EDT.

As the Airbus A319 was en route to Florida, flight attendants alerted the cockpit crew to a disturbance involving a passenger in row 9.

UNRULY PASSENGERS COULD BE BANNED FOR LIFE FROM MULTIPLE AIRLINES UNDER NEW PROPOSAL

According to Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System (ACARS) datalink logs published by aviation website AirLive, the lead flight attendant reported that a female passenger in seat 9D had completely undressed and engaged in indecent acts in view of nearby passengers.

The ACARS message stated the incident was required to be reported to American Airlines’ Integrated Operations Center and that law enforcement should be requested.

FRONTIER PASSENGERS TACKLE MAN WHO ALLEGEDLY CHOKED OFF-DUTY FLIGHT ATTENDANT, TRIED TO OPEN DOOR MID-FLIGHT

The flight continued to Miami without diverting and arrived at Gate D2 in Terminal N, according to flight tracking service Flightera. AirLive reported that law enforcement officers were waiting at the gate and that the passenger was taken into custody.

It remains unclear what specific measures cabin crew took during the flight to manage the disturbance.

Fox News Digital has reached out to American Airlines, the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office and Miami International Airport for comment.
